turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey, you got a sec? I need to vent about the DNS switch yesterday.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh no, what happened? I saw the incident page go off around 2 AM.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, so I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was actually ready. I thought the health checks would pass, but they didn't.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, you flipped DNS without waiting for the green light? That's a classic.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I know, I know. And of course, traffic hit a cluster that could not serve it. Every single region went down for hours.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hours? That's brutal. Did you at least roll back fast?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Rollback was messy because the old cluster was already decommissioned. We had to rebuild it on the fly. The outage lasted for hours and hit every region, including APAC.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Yikes. So what's the lesson here? I'm guessing you're not doing that again.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Definitely not. From now on, I'm waiting for the cluster health check before switching DNS. No exceptions.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw you pushed the new cluster migration over the weekend. How did it go?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Surprisingly smooth. This time I waited for the health check, and traffic moved over without a hitch. Zero errors.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice! So you finally learned your lesson, huh?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Ha, yeah. Also, I enabled autoscaling on the instances this time, so we won't get caught with our pants down if there's a spike.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good call. But I heard you also did the schema migration in the same window? That's risky.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I ran the migration in a maintenance window, so it was planned. But honestly, I didn't take a backup first. That was a mistake.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, you migrated the schema without a backup? What if something went wrong?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Well, something did go wrong. The migration corrupted customer records. We had to restore from a snapshot that was two days old.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Oh man. So the migration finished without locking anything, but it still broke data. That's the worst kind of failure.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. No locks, no downtime, but silent corruption. We only caught it because a support ticket came in about missing orders.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw you updated the runbook. Looks like you added a new policy about deployment windows.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, after the last two incidents, I adopted a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window. No more last-minute changes without a full checklist.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: What's in the checklist? Just curious.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: First, mandatory backup before any schema change. Second, health check must be green for at least 15 minutes before DNS switch. Third, autoscaling must be enabled and tested.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's solid. So you're basically making sure we never repeat the 'point DNS at a dead cluster' fiasco.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Exactly. And I'm also adding a step to verify data integrity after any migration, not just rely on the migration finishing without locking anything.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Smart. I'll make sure my team follows it too. Thanks for owning this.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: No problem. I'd rather have a boring, safe process than another 3 AM page.
